not_reproduced_exactly: Different host: Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.30GHz (family 6 model 173), kernel 6.18.44-fc-v310, vs 2.10GHz / fc-v185 on 2 Nov. Upstream CPython (identical python3.13 sha256 and upstream source bytes) ran 26-36% faster per repair (52-53% on the 8 KB valid string), so raw percentage changes mix host and software.

Upstream came from the PyPI 0.64.1 wheel (sha256 matches PyPI; 22 sources match the ace9b23c manifest) rather than a git checkout, so the runner's source identity for that variant is the Pystachy checkout (probe scripts); the wheel was hashed before/after separately.
CPython variants used PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX in scratch and the JIT used PYSTACHY_CACHE in scratch, to keep the checkout unmodified; neither is inside the timed loops.
The runner now sets PYSTACHY_PROGRAM_CACHE=0 for every process (the program cache did not exist on 2 Nov), so port-jit remains lli ORC JIT.
The 150-process size sweep was not repeated; the nine workloads (180 processes) were run twice.
The checkout's HEAD a6f2956f adds only research/ commits to ce8c887f.
